findings.title: Exit 0 does not mean SAT, UNSAT, or even a completed decision
observations: SAT control and both UNSAT controls exit 0.
anchor-residual-ordered prints s TIMELIMIT but exits 0; other timeouts exit 4.
findings.consequence: Shell success checks can silently misclassify an unfinished run. The frontend execs the solver and cannot normalize the result afterward.
findings.recommendation: Use the explicit s status line as the decision field. Keep raw exit status separately, require a terminal status, and classify timeout/unknown/error independently. Do not change vendored code.

findings.title: No end-to-end candidate or UNSAT-certificate acceptance path
observations: Engine execs the solver without decoding or validating a SAT assignment.
RoundingSat help defaults --print-sol to 0. All these solver runs explicitly request 1.
Proof logging was deliberately disabled; no UNSAT result here is certified.
findings.consequence: A solver status alone cannot safely become research evidence, even if a future run decides a nontrivial slice.
findings.recommendation: Separate solving from acceptance: retain assignment/proof, reconstruct all 43 vertices, exhaustively check all 5-subsets, and integrate an approved independent proof checker before exclusion claims.

findings.title: Nauty is a graph6 parser in the engine, not solver symmetry reduction
observations: First and second B graphs both have automorphism group size 1 and 24 orbits.
Canonicalizing B changes the anchor search trace but still times out.
The engine emits all labelled A constraints without an A symmetry breaker. Degree ordering also times out.
findings.consequence: Canonical B labelling does not remove permutations of the 18 unknown A vertices. A designated 4-anchor still leaves permutations of its 14 other A vertices.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate symmetry handling for the combined unknown A/cross structure, with a coverage argument. Cheap internal-degree ordering is incomplete and is not a demonstrated speedup here.

findings.title: The local PB solver has no LP backend
observations: Configured local Release build has soplex:STRING=OFF.
Every measured hard run reports LP calls 0.
The help still lists LP controls and --lp default 1.
findings.consequence: Linear constraints are handled by PB/CDCL propagation and cutting planes, not an LP relaxation in this build.
findings.recommendation: Expose solver build capabilities in experiment metadata. Compare with an LP-enabled local build only after obtaining approval for any missing dependency/download; no LP performance claim follows from these runs.

findings.title: Stronger restrictions change per-conflict cost, not just search space
observations: At equal 8-second internal CPU budgets: default 137966 conflicts, zero excess 106350, fixed x138 zero excess 41990.
Fixed x138 learns 16723 general constraints versus 0 in the default run.
All 9 nontrivial comparisons time out. Disabling counting propagation does not decide the anchor instance.
findings.consequence: Fewer variables or stronger equations cannot be assumed to imply faster solving. Conflict counts alone are not a progress/completeness metric.
findings.recommendation: Benchmark repeated instances and deterministic work counters with fixed scope. Keep runtime, learned-constraint mix and memory, not just conflict throughput. No tuning default is justified by this small sample.

findings.title: Scoped graph constraints require external OPB surgery
observations: The CLI exposes aggregate interval endpoints and zero excess but no fixed edge literals, designated independent set, anchor degree constraints, or residual degree ordering.
Experiments added 14 anchor rows, 96 arbitrary fixed-cross-edge rows, and degree-order rows outside the engine.
Arbitrary pinned incidences already force an explicit 5-vertex obstruction: {'type': 'I5', 'vertices': ['A0', 'A1', 'A2', 'B7', 'B11']}
findings.consequence: Ad hoc text augmentation couples experiments to variable numbering and header maintenance. An easy UNSAT slice can simply be inconsistent input, not evidence of difficult-branch feasibility.
findings.recommendation: A small typed experiment-cut interface using the existing builder would improve usability. Record every cut and whether it is implied, a covered symmetry choice, or an arbitrary restriction; do not promote these artificial pins into production defaults.

findings.title: Late contradiction and option discovery forces avoidable generation and parsing
observations: Impossible pivot cap generates a 28549175-byte OPB before UNSAT at parsing, with zero search decisions.
An invalid forwarded solver option is discovered only after a complete default OPB is generated.
All core rows are built before any optional bound component.
findings.consequence: Obvious input contradictions and execution mistakes still incur model construction, serialization and sometimes full core parsing.
findings.recommendation: Preflight fixed pivot/bounds and solver availability before large generation, while preserving an explicit infeasible-model mode when requested. Separate generate/solve commands so tuning does not regenerate identical models.

findings.title: One-shot frontend lacks catalogue scheduling and reproducible run records
observations: Frontend handles one B record per invocation. read_record scans from the beginning for each --index.
OPB metadata records variable map and B graph6 but not active constraint options, source/tool hashes or artificial scope.
Experiment drivers had to add resource limits, raw logs, status parsing, hashing and compressed model retention.
Solver path is baked into the engine at build time.
findings.consequence: Naive index-by-index batch use performs quadratic catalogue scanning and cannot safely resume/aggregate a decision frontier. Moving the checkout or swapping solver builds needs manual care.
findings.recommendation: Use a sequential catalogue iterator or index, explicit solver path, and a manifest-driven external supervisor with separate model/scope/attempt IDs and resumable undecided cases. Preserve exec signal behavior for the low-level frontend.

findings.title: Order-18 generation is not yet a measured complete enumeration strategy
observations: The small n6/e6 connected generator completes and countg reports 13 graphs.
Count-only K4-free/I5-free n18/e84 generation hits the 5-second watchdog without a completed count.
findings.consequence: The tiny control validates local tool plumbing, not scalability or coverage at order 18. Timeout gives no bound on remaining work.
findings.recommendation: Measure split-job sizes and retain exact res/mod settings before using generation as a coverage source. No catalogue completeness or nonexistence conclusion is drawn here.

illustrative_catalogue_arithmetic.warning: Arithmetic illustration only, not a projection that 8 seconds decides any record. Most measured cases remained undecided.
